{{Short description|Type of diagram}}

[[File:Sina plot ver1.png|320px|thumb|right|A violin plot (on the left) and a sina plot (on the right) for the same sample.]]

A '''sina plot''' is a type of diagram in which numerical data are depicted by points distributed in such a way that the width of the point distribution is proportional to the [[Kernel density estimation|kernel density]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sidiropoulos |first=Nikos |last2=Sohi |first2=Sina Hadi |last3=Pedersen |first3=Thomas Lin |last4=Porse |first4=Bo Torben |last5=Winther |first5=Ole |last6=Rapin |first6=Nicolas |last7=Bagger |first7=Frederik Otzen |date=2018-07-03 |title=SinaPlot: An Enhanced Chart for Simple and Truthful Representation of Single Observations Over Multiple Classes |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10618600.2017.1366914 |journal=Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics |language=en |volume=27 |issue=3 |pages=673–676 |doi=10.1080/10618600.2017.1366914 |issn=1061-8600|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="wilke">{{Cite book |last=Wilke |first=Claus |title=Fundamentals of data visualization: a primer on making informative and compelling figures |date=2019 |publisher=O'Reilly |isbn=978-1-4920-3108-6 |edition=First |location=Beijing Boston Farnham Sebastopol Tokyo}}</ref> Sina plots are similar to [[violin plot]]s, but while violin plots depict kernel density, sina plots depict the points themselves. In some situations, sina plots may be preferable to violin plots, because sina plots contain more information.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-03 |title=Sinaplot vs Violin plot - Why Sinaplot is better than Violinplot in R |url=https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sinaplot-vs-violin-plot-why-sinaplot-is-better-than-violinplot-in-r/ |access-date=2023-11-18 |website=GeeksforGeeks |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=datavizpyr |date=2021-03-28 |title=Sinaplot vs Violin plot: Why Sinaplot is better than Violinplot - Data Viz with Python and R |url=https://datavizpyr.com/sinaplot-vs-violin-plot-why-sinaplot-is-better-than-violinplot/,%20https://datavizpyr.com/sinaplot-vs-violin-plot-why-sinaplot-is-better-than-violinplot/ |access-date=2023-11-18 |language=en-US}}</ref>

The term "sina plot" is intended to recognize the contributions of Sina Hadi Sohi, a student at the University of Copenhagen in Denmark. Sina created the original code that researchers at the university used to generate these plots.<ref name="wilke"/>

There are a number of ways to create sina plots, in particular:

* The [[ggplot2]] library of the [[R (programming language)|R programming language]] used together with the ggforce package.<ref>https://ggforce.data-imaginist.com/reference/geom_sina.html</ref>
* The sinaplot library of the R programming language.<ref>https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sinaplot/vignettes/SinaPlot.html</ref>
* The plotnine library of the [[Python (programming language)|Python programming language]].<ref>https://plotnine.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/plotnine.geoms.geom_sina.html</ref>
